attempts.text:
```json
{
  "map": true,
  "subject": {
    "columns": ["protein_id"],
    "resolver": "pharos_protein_gene",
    "category": "biolink:Gene"
  },
  "object": {
    "columns": ["go_id"],
    "resolver": "curie",
    "category": "biolink:GeneOntologyClass",
    "name_column": "go_term_text"
  },
  "predicate": "biolink:involved_in",
  "association_category": "biolink:GeneToGeneOntologyTermAssociation",
  "knowledge_level": "knowledge_assertion",
  "agent_type": "not_provided",
  "primary_knowledge_source": "infores:goa",
  "qualifiers": {},
  "edge_properties": ["evidence", "goeco", "assigned_by", "go_term_text"],
  "keep_if": null,
  "split_by": "go_type",
  "by_value": {
    "Process": {"predicate": "biolink:involved_in"},
    "Function": {"predicate": "biolink:enables"},
    "Component": {"predicate": "biolink:located_in"}
  },
  "notes": "Each row is one GO annotation of a human reviewed UniProt protein, mapped to its gene via pharos_protein_gene. The GO aspect (go_type) selects the predicate: Process to involved_in, Function to enables, Component to located_in. The evidence code (IEA, IDA, ISS and so on) is kept as an edge property, not used to pick the knowledge level, since the evidence mix spans automated and experimental claims. Agent type is not_provided for the same reason. Using knowledge_assertion is a choice a reader may question, since the IEA rows are electronic inferences. The source is infores:goa, the GO annotation resource. The go_id values are already compact GO CURIEs, so the curie resolver is used without transformation."
}
```
